item.title: Individual Project
item.description: Individual Project # This is your own project, separate from the team project. Use one individual GitHub Pages website throughout the semester and register its link in ML Class Hub. Improve that same site at midterm and final. The Hub assignment will identify the required dataset, label mappings, and submission details once staff configure it. CIFAR-10 is an example, not a required dataset. Dates appear on the course schedule.

item.title: Individual Website Template
item.description: Individual Project Website Template # This is a rendered Markdown example of the website’s required shape. For the individual project, follow the headings and subsection order exactly on one website. Replace every instruction and blank with your own work; do not omit a required subsection, even if its answer is that a result was unavailable and why. Your methods and findings will differ from another student’s. Do not copy sample results or assume a sample dataset is assigned.

item.title: Team Website Template
item.description: Team Project Website Template # This is a rendered Markdown example of the required team-report shape, not a sample project to copy. Keep these core headings on the same team website from proposal through final so TAs can find the required evidence. Teams may add subsections, improve the layout, and build richer interactive features or software beyond this starting structure; do not replace or hide the required content. At proposal, write a plan; at midterm, replace plans with work completed so far; at final, revise the same sections to report the full evidence.

item.title: Categories
item.description: Grading Categories # The required course components total 100%. There is no final exam. Teams can earn up to 5 additional course percentage points for exceptional optional work beyond the required team project, for a maximum course score of 105%. The bonus criteria explain what qualifies. Component Course weight Quizzes 1–14 15% Midterm exam 10% Individual project 35% Team project 40% Total 100% Quiz 0 is required preparation but carries no course-grade weight.

item.title: Collection
item.description: GT Resources # For any resources related to Student Engagement and Wellbeing such as Dean of Student’s contacts, Library, etc., please refer to this LINK Class Resources # Required Course Materials # No textbook will be required for this course, however you are strongly encouraged to complete the readings indicated for each class. You may also find the following books very helpful: Learning from data, by Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa Pattern recognition and machine learning, by Christopher Bishop Machine learning, by Tom Mitchell Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques, by Jiawei Han, Micheline Kamber, and Jian Pei The Elements of Statistical Learning, by Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, and Jerome Friedman Deep Learning, by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville Other resources, such as machine learning toolboxes and datasets, will be provided throughout the course.

item.title: Course Overview
item.description: Course Overview # Important CSE students should note that CS 7641 is not allowed as a substitute for the CSE core course CSE 6740, and that they cannot get credit for both CSE 6740 and CS 7641. Course Description # This course introduces techniques in machine learning with an emphasis on algorithms and their applications to real-world data. We will investigate the following question: how to computationally extract useful knowledge from data for decision making and task support!

item.title: General
item.description: General Course Policies # Online participation and course materials # Core lectures are pre-recorded; live lecture attendance is not required. Study the assigned videos and notes, complete assessments within their availability windows, and work on both the individual and team projects. The schedule also links interactive visualizations and demonstrations when available. Course-created videos, notes, assessment questions, and code are for enrolled students. Do not redistribute them outside the course without written permission.

item.title: Team Proposal
item.description: Team Project Proposal # Write the proposal on the same team website you will use through midterm and final. Register the team and link in ML Class Hub by the course schedule deadline. This is for the team project, not the individual project. No proposal video or separate proposal website is required. Choose a feasible question # Identify a meaningful ML question, a lawful and obtainable dataset, a simple baseline, and a measurable outcome.

item.title: Office Hours
item.description: Online Office Hours # Office hours are optional online help sessions. They do not replace scheduled project reviews. Joining a session # A TA announces the session in an Ed thread with the time and any focus topic. Reply with a short, specific question and what you have tried. Do not post private information, complete code, grades, or confidential project data. The TA answers in the thread when useful to the class, or sends a private meeting link when screen sharing or individual discussion is needed.

item.title: Team Midterm Review
item.description: Team Midterm Website Review and TA Meeting # Update the same team website before the meeting with your assigned TA. This is the team midterm checkpoint, not a separate report or video. The course schedule gives the review window; the individual project’s video is a separate requirement. Update the proposal, do not start over # Keep the proposal’s section headings and turn plans into evidence: Introduction and related work: refine the question and explain any justified change since the proposal.

item.title: Team Final Report
item.description: Team Final Report, Website, and TA Interview # Complete a paper-style report on the same team website, with supporting code and reproduction instructions. The TA interview is in the two-week final-review window; the completed website is due on the last instructional day in the course schedule. Keep the same ML Class Hub team link. The individual final is separate; see Individual Project. Use the rendered team website template as the minimum report structure, including the required interactive visualization.

item.title: Bonus
item.description: Optional Team-Project Bonus # The required course components total 100%. A team can earn up to 5 additional course percentage points for exceptional work beyond the complete required team project, making 105% the maximum possible course score. The individual project has no separate bonus. Both CS 4641 · Undergraduate and CS 7641 · Graduate teams have the same five-point bonus ceiling, but bonus work must exceed the requirements for their course level.

item.title: Awards and Examples
item.description: Project Awards and Examples # These awards recognize exceptional individual and team projects. Awards are distinct from course grades and the optional team-project bonus; an award is not needed for full credit or bonus credit. Every completed project is eligible for consideration; no separate award application is required. The final website and interview are the evidence reviewed. See Grading Categories for the course-grade weights. What makes a project stand out # A clear, important question and an honest account of related work.
